programme.title: Kahani Kismat Ki
programme.desc: A reformed man tries to make an honest living for himself and his family after his jail term. His life takes an ugly turn when a woman claims him to be her husband and he is also framed for murder.

programme.title: Koyelaanchal
programme.desc: An honest IAS officer rises against the atrocities of a brutal mafioso. In retaliation, the mafioso sends a deadly human weapon to kill the officer, who instead ends up abducting his child.

programme.title: Ek Lahoo
programme.desc: Ashok and Lakshmi share an ideal brother-sister relationship. They find their perfect matches and lead a happily married life until Ashok's wife's aunt comes into their life and creates mayhem.

programme.title: Love Mocktail
programme.desc: After rescuing a woman, Adi reminisces about his love life and tells her about all the heartbreaks he endured in his quest to find his true love.

programme.title: Agnivarsha
programme.desc: In a kingdom stricken with drought, two rival priests, Yavakri and Parvasu, try to appease the rain god, Indra. However, their efforts result in adultery, treachery and bloodshed.

programme.title: Jaan Se Pyaara
programme.desc: Inspector Jai arrests Guman only to release him after he threatens to destroy the city. Later, Jai's brother, who has a cognitive disability, gets abducted in return for a mysterious bag.

programme.title: Kaali Topi Laal Roomaal
programme.desc: Commando Vijay arrests a terrorist, Master DD. However, he realises that Master DD is just a pawn and tries to find the real culprit.

programme.title: Pyar Ke Kabil
programme.desc: Kiran and Jyoti are twins who were separated after their parents uncoupled. Years later, they meet accidentally at a picnic and decide to exchange places in an effort to reunite their parents.

programme.title: Aakhri Ghulam
programme.desc: Bheema, his father Dinu and generations of their family have been slaves of the wealthy Thakurs. One day, he challenges their authority and invites trouble for himself in the process.

programme.title: Kusthi
programme.desc: Jeeva runs away to the city to avoid an arranged marriage. Soon, he befriends Singam, a local goon, after which, they get involved in many mishaps together.

programme.title: Salta Diya
programme.desc: A rich man's wife and a thief's wife simultaneously give birth to twin sons, from which two of them get exchanged. Years later, an unexpected event leads them to swap places once again.

programme.title: Love Mocktail 2
programme.desc: With the semblance of leading a normal life, Adi struggles with the loss of his wife, Nidhi. However, Sihi, a charming young woman, enters as a glimmer of hope when she commits to helping Adi.

programme.title: Mast
programme.desc: Kittu is madly in love with Malika, an actress, and travels to her house in Mumbai from Pune after his father scolds him for his decreasing exam scores.

programme.title: Juaari
programme.desc: Vijay, a young man, resorts to gambling in order to free his lover, Anita, who is held captive by Sanga. He soon runs out of luck when he gets arrested.

programme.title: 15th August
programme.desc: Nagpal kills Chaudhry and his son, Ram, a military officer. Chaudhry's second son, Vikram, vows to destroy Nagpal who is all set to become the Chief Minister on the upcoming Indian Independence Day.

programme.title: Farz
programme.desc: Gopal, a secret agent, investigates the death of his colleague who possessed evidence against a known terrorist. Gopal and Kamla embark on a journey to find the traitor.

programme.title: 16 December
programme.desc: Four Indian Revenue Service officers are assigned to intercept and arrest a group of Pakistani terrorists. The terrorists plot to detonate a nuclear bomb in New Delhi and the IRS must stop them.

programme.title: Demon
programme.desc: Vignesh Shivan has scary dreams that bother him a lot. However, the strange things in his dreams make him worry and affect his mind.

programme.title: Chalte Chalte
programme.desc: Geeta is admitted to a mental hospital after her lover passes away tragically. Later, she gains her senses, only to find him alive and in love with another woman.

programme.title: Humse Hai Zamana
programme.desc: Ravindra and Gowri, who belong to rival factions, are sworn enemies. After being imprisoned and learning that his brother was killed, Gowri goes after Ravindra's sister, Preeti, as revenge.

programme.title: Prithipal Singh...A Story
programme.desc: Disappointed with his Olympic bronze medal, Prithipal Singh quits hockey and joins a university. However, things get worse for him when he is accused of murdering a student.

Animated adventure, with the voices of Eva Gabor, Phil Harris and Scatman Crothers.

programme.title: The Mighty Ducks

However, he comes to appreciate his new role and things finally start to look up for the team. Comedy, starring Emilio Estevez, Joss Ackland, Lane Smith and Joshua Jackson.

programme.title: Cars 2
programme.desc: Racing car Lightning McQueen heads overseas to compete in an international grand prix, with events in Britain, Japan and Italy. Pixar animated adventure sequel, with the voices of Owen Wilson and Michael Caine.

programme.title: The Parent Trap
programme.desc: Identical twin sisters who are unaware of each other's existence meet by accident. They decide to join forces in a bid to reunite their estranged parents, and switch places to get the warring couple to kiss and make up. Remake of the 1961 Disney comedy, starring Dennis Quaid, Natasha Richardson, Elaine Hendrix and Lindsay Lohan in a dual role.

His mission leads him on another globe-trotting treasure hunt that uncovers a secret conspiracy. Adventure sequel, starring Nicolas Cage, Helen Mirren, Ed Harris, Harvey Keitel and Jon Voight.

programme.title: Hitman: Agent 47
programme.desc: The latest in a long line of genetically engineered clones bred to be the perfect assassin takes on a mission that strikes close to home. A corporation intends to use the technology that created him to build an army of superhuman killers. As the assassin fights to bring them down, he uncovers the dark secrets surrounding his origin. Action thriller, starring Rupert Friend, Hannah Ware and Zachary Quinto.

programme.title: Veronica Guerin
programme.desc: Fact-based drama about crime reporter Veronica Guerin, who set out to expose Ireland's crime lords but ended up paying the ultimate price. The film opens with the journalist's assassination, then looks back to trace her attempts to establish a link between Dublin's drug trade and infamous gangster Martin Cahill in the mid-1990s. Starring Cate Blanchett, Gerard McSorley, Ciaran Hinds and Brenda Fricker.

She pursues the lead role in a production of Swan Lake, but the director convinces her she will only be capable of dancing the part if she embraces her darker impulses. This leads her into a destructive relationship with a rival that threatens her sanity. Drama, starring an Oscar-winning Natalie Portman. With Mila Kunis, Vincent Cassel and Winona Ryder.

Comedy, starring Isla Fisher, Hugh Dancy, Krysten Ritter and Joan Cusack.

Fantasy comedy, starring Adam Sandler, Keri Russell, Guy Pearce and Russell Brand.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the last chance for the Central Region chefs to impress, with the dessert course. Only two chefs can go through to cook for the judges so with everything to play for, who will plate up perfection and who will be sent packing?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two remaining Central Region chefs cook their entire menus again for the judges - Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. They'll be joined by former chair of the Women's Institute Helen Carey, who will help decide who will have the glory of representing the region in the National Finals.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the starter course, and 8 of the finest chefs in the country are battling it out to plate up impeccable dishes worthy of the Women's Institute. The judges are joined by WI Calendar Girl Angela Baker, but after Oliver reveals that this year it will be much tougher to make it onto the judge's shortlist, who will keep their cool and secure a place?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the battle for the fish course, and those chefs who didn't make it onto the shortlist with their starters are hoping to do better. The judges are joined by a WI president, Kristy Bowen, who knows the impeccable standards the Institute will expect.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's main course day, the half-way point in Finals Week, and those chefs who have yet to get a dish on the shortlist are feeling the heat. With only dishes judged to be perfect in with a chance at reaching the WI banquet, the standards are higher than ever before.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's a battle for dessert, and the last chance for the 8 regional champions to get a dish in contention for the final banquet. Those who've failed to make the judges shortlist so far are going all out. Joining the judges is author of the WI centenary cookbook Mary Gwynn.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The banquet is finally here. It's the culmination of months of hard work as the winning chefs strive to plate up perfect dishes for the ladies of the Women's Institute, at London's historic Draper's Hall where pioneers of the WI once gathered.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three top chefs from Scotland are out to impress this week's veteran judge and be crowned Scottish champion. Adam Handling has already won a number of industry awards and is full of confidence. His starter sets out to take the diner on a tour of the UKs best producers. He's up against Michael Bremner, who is hoping to impress with contemporary ingredients including Birch sap and Douglas fir oil. Ally McGrath is celebrating his nation's finest produce and making his very own version of haggis.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three newcomers to the competition create their fish dishes in a bid to be crowned Scottish champion. The standard is so high the veteran judge is moved to tears.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Ally McGrath has been keeping the veteran judge entertained with his very individual approach. Also, the highly competitive Adam Handling has been showcasing the finest produce grown and caught in and around the UK in his menu. Once again Michael Bremner is out to show how inventive he can be.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: One chef will go home and today the veteran judge finds himself with a difficult decision to make. Inventive Chef Michael Bremner is recreating the Scottish deserts of his childhood, Adam Handling is sticking with his trademark Asian flavours and Ally McGrath is tempering chocolate for the very first time.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Scotland's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges for the very first time. Both chefs have decided to make changes to some of their dishes, taking on board criticisms made during the week by the veteran judge.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Chef Josh Eggleton is back for a third time. Last year he made the national finals when his starter was shortlisted for the banquet, this year he intends to go one step further and cook at the banquet. One of his rivals last time, Jude Kereama is also back and out to do better than he did previously. The third competitor is newcomer Chris Wheeler who is originally from Swanage in Dorset.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: There are some exciting dishes on the menu as the three chefs from the South West tackle the fish course. Chef Josh Eggleton is hoping to impress with an original take on Bolognese, just one of six elements on his complex fish dish.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the main course and Chef Chris Wheeler is out to show just how theatrical he can be, his ideas are surprising everyone in the kitchen. No one knows quite what to expect and the veteran chef is hoping it tastes as good as it looks.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the dessert course and it is Josh Eggleton who has come up with the most ambitious dessert. He is creating his own self-serve ice cream made from vegetables, he is making everything from scratch including toppings and syrups.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the head to head and the South West region's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort. They are joined by guest judge, journalist and restaurant critic, Grace Dent.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Two newcomers to the competition are challenging reigning North West champion Matt Worswick. Adam Reid is Head Chef for one of the UK's leading culinary talents, and Kim Woodward who made history when she was appointed Head Chef at the Savoy Grill.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and reigning North West champion Matt Worswick has reason to be confident. However, Kim's confident she has got one up on Matt by baking her own black bread unlike Matt who's taking a shortcut.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the main course of the North West Regional heat and the scores mean this is a crucial round. Matt Worswick may be the reigning champion but he is not yet assured of a place cooking for the judges and he is feeling the strain.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the three North West competitors are getting creative, producing some of the most original and stunning desserts. All three chefs are working in a hot kitchen, the tension is palpable, and this time one chef will go home.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two chefs are cooking for judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton, and guest judge Lady Claire MacDonald OBE. There are stand out dishes from both chefs making it a difficult contest to judge.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three of the finest chefs from Wales are competing to be crowned champion. Two chefs are back for a second time: Phil Carmichael, from Cowbridge, South Wales, is Executive Chef at Berners Tavern in London and Adam Bannister, is chef and co-owner of Slice in his home city of Swansea. Adam was crowed Welsh champion last year so this year Phil is back with something to prove. He plans to go home raising the flag for Wales. The third chef is newcomer Andrew Birch, also from Swansea.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and newcomer Andrew Birch is confident, he is passionate about seafood. He is celebrating the cockle which is harvested near his home city of Swansea. Adam Bannister has created an alter ego, Captain Bannister for his modern take on the old boil in the bag fish dinners and Phil has chosen to revamp the classic prawn cocktail.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Phil Carmichael is serving up his version of an OBE, a refined take on onions, bacon and egg. Adam is planning to serve up Wild boar on a spit, while Andrew turns up the heat when he combines strong Japanese flavours with a traditional roast.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the dessert course and one chef will go home. Phil Carmichael is determined it won't be him but not everything is going to plan when he tackles his 'Cup of Tea for Ma'am'. One of the accompaniments to his earl grey panna cotta just won't work. He has to make a difficult decision.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the head to head. The two highest scoring chefs from Wales are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort who are joined by guest judge, blogger and food writer Rosie Birkett.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three newcomers are competing to become regional champion. Daniel Smith, a former head chef for the Roux brothers, now runs his own restaurant in his beloved home county of Norfolk. Andrew Scott's worked with the best in the business, and he's concentrating on telling powerful stories as well as delivering perfect flavours. Danny Gill is a former head chef at Daniel Clifford's two star restaurant Midsummer House.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the chefs are using some of the UK's best seafood: lobster, salmon and Cornish crab. Danny Gill is a chef who likes to use the very latest equipment to create the most intense flavours. He's going to great lengths to maximise the taste of his cucumber consommé and it is causing a lot of interest in the kitchen.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Two chefs are cooking venison. Danny Gill is making a venison wellington, inspired by his Dad, a former RAF chef who has served up Wellington for royalty at many air force banquets. While Andrew Scott has sourced his venison from the Queen's Scottish estate, Balmoral.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: This week three chefs from the central region are fighting to be crowned champion. One competitor will go home, only the two highest scoring chefs will make it through to the judging chamber. Danny Gill is facing his toughest day yet, choosing to make a staggering eight elements for his imaginative dessert.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The Central region's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort, for the very first time. Joining them in the chamber is guest judge Enam Ali MBE, a food entrepreneur who set up The British Curry Awards.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three of the most exciting talents from London and the South East region are competing for a place in the National Finals. Head chef Mark Froydenlund runs Marcus Wareing's two star restaurant. Russell Bateman is head Chef at The Grove in Hertfordshire and Ronnie Murray who heads up the Hix Restaurant group.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and chef Russell Bateman is celebrating the diversity of his beloved home town of London - by combining lobster with jerk spices for an ambitious fish course with seven key elements. Ronnie Murray's taking a risk with an ingredient which is close to the veteran judge's heart...and is planning to serve it at three different temperatures warm, deep fried and frozen. And two Michelin starred Mark Froydenlund is planning a novel way to present his dish.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the all-important main course and returning contender Mark Froydenlund is banking on it being his strongest dish. Russell Bateman is creating a beef dish, and Ronnie Murray's mixing a crown of lamb with a curried filling.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the final chance for three of London & South East's most competitive and talented chefs to get through to the judging chamber, today the veteran judge will send one chef home.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the head to head and the two highest scoring chefs from the London and South East region are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort. Joining this week as guest judge is Kevin Gould, an award winning food writer.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Mini Patel is back for a second attempt at the north east regional title but he is competing against two young newcomers, Tommy Banks and Chris Archer. Last year, Mini went home after the dessert course, so he is hoping to keep better control of his nerves this year.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and two chefs, Tommy and Mini, have very similar ingredients - both are cooking mackerel. But Mini is trying an original beetroot sorbet while Tommy is using wild woodruff and oyster leaf from his own garden. Chris Archer has chosen the king of the sea, turbot, but there is controversy in the kitchen.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and two chefs, Tommy and Mini, have very similar ingredients - both are cooking mackerel. But Mini is trying an original beetroot sorbet while Tommy is using wild woodruff and oyster leaf from his own garden. Chris Archer has chosen the king of the sea, turbot, but there is controversy in the kitchen.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the main course of the north east region and overnight there has been a dramatic development. It is a tough and emotional day for the chefs as they react to the news but they battle on in a bid to present a perfect dish with venison and wagyu-angus beef - the meat of the day.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is a highly emotional day for one of the chefs as he prepares a dish which is inspired by and a tribute to his own great Briton, his late grandfather. But all is not going to plan and the chef ends up making one key element three times in a bid to achieve perfection.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two chefs are cooking for judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton for the very first time. Joining them as guest judge is John Williams MBE, the executive head chef at The Ritz, the only hotel to hold a royal warrant for banqueting.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is Chris McGowan's third time however, he is facing tough competition from Mark Abbott, head chef at Daniel Clifford's 2 Michelin star restaurant, Midsummer House, and also from Eddie Attwell who has just completed a year as head chef at Ardtara Country House in Upperlands.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Mark Abbott is pushing himself again plating up a complex fish course of the very finest produce. He is calling it Shellsational but at the last minute he forgets a key element. Returning chef Chris McGowan is refining cod and chips and Eddie Attwell is getting classical with the king of the sea, turbot.The repartee is relentless as the chefs jostle for top place on the leader board. Once again there is plenty of emotion as the veteran chef delivers the scores.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the main course and returning Chef Chris McGowan is feeling confident but part of his dish involves making his own venison sausages to serve with a venison rack, and getting it all done in time is straining his emotions. Eddie Attwell is also serving the meat but with a traditional Northern Irish dish called Dock pudding. Mark Abbott is pushing himself again, he is using wagyu beef and serving it with tongue and corn cooked in a variety of ways.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The three chefs from Northern Ireland are cooking their desserts and one chef is on course for a historic score, he could beat his boss - a veteran of GBM - and achieve more marks than anyone has done throughout the history of the competition.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the head to head. The two highest scoring chefs from Northern Ireland are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort who are joined by guest judge, restaurant critic and Editor-at-Large of the Independent, Amol Rajan.

programme.title: 7 Up: The Story
programme.desc: In 1964, ITV broadcast a film about 14 seven-year-olds, which became the longest-running documentary series ever. It set out to prove that Britain was divided by the class system and that these children's futures had been decided by the street they were born on. This programme looks at the year 7 Up was made, the idea behind it, and what the subjects hoped for in a Britain about to change around them.

programme.desc: Tim Shaw and Fuzz Townshend restore a Triumph TR4 belonging to a man left unable to drive it by a stroke. However, it may be the biggest job they have ever taken on

programme.title: Inside Melbourne Airport
programme.desc: Brad has just 90 minutes to turn around an Air India flight. A kangaroo keeps Trent on his toes, and baggage handler Brodie battles jams

programme.title: Air Crash Investigation
programme.desc: During monsoon season at a treacherous tabletop runway in India, the crew of Flight 1344 runs off the tarmac and their Boeing 737-800 plunges into a gorge

programme.title: Hitler's Last Stand
programme.desc: Outgunned and cut off, a ragged band of survivors from a Canadian regiment make their desperate last stand in a farmhouse during the bloodiest day of the war since Dieppe

programme.title: Planes that Changed History
programme.desc: The Chinook, a heavy-lift helicopter that rewrote the rules of aviation. Its bent airframe and tandem rotors gave it a huge lift capability, transforming US military strategy

programme.title: Lost Treasures of Egypt
programme.desc: Archaeologists are on the trail of Tutankhamun. To piece together his story, they search his tomb for secrets previously missed

programme.title: Ice Road Rescue
programme.desc: Thord and Bjoern rescue a truck that threatens to tip, while Jo Roger looks to save a snow plough - before a second truck crashes in the same spot

programme.title: Nazi Megastructures
programme.desc: The German campaign across Tunisia, Libya and Egypt, under the command of Erwin Rommel, which would push the allies to their limit and change the course of the war

programme.title: Air Crash Investigation
programme.desc: How investigations into a plane that nosedived into the runway at Russia's Rostov airport uncovered one of the most lethal traps in aviation

programme.title: How the Tudors Lost Their Heads
programme.desc: Suzannah Lipscomb and Dan Snow explore evidence that reveals a different side to Anne Boleyn, whose ideas transformed England and whose reputation deserves reassessing

programme.title: Bloody Tales of the Tower
programme.desc: Suzannah Lipscomb and Joe Crowley examine the evidence and report on the intrigues that led to three royal deaths, detailing the sometimes salacious accusations levelled at Anne Boleyn, Catherine Howard and Lady Arabella Seymour. Henry VIII's chief minister Thomas Cromwell informed the monarch of gossip about Anne and court musician Mark Smeaton, but allegations at her public trial included adultery with five men, incest with her brother George and treason. Rumours of relationships with distant cousin Francis Dereham and Thomas Culpeper led to Catherine Howard's execution, while Lady Arabella, a serious threat to the ruling Stuart dynasty, is thought to have committed suicide against a backdrop of a cross-dressing noblewoman and two escapes from the Tower

programme.title: Mysteries of Ancient Medicine
programme.sub-title: Relitto Del Pozzino, Ancient Opium, Liang Tebo
programme.desc: A Roman shipwreck reveals the oldest known medical tablets, poppy-shaped jars in a Canaanite tomb trace the roots of opioid use and a Stone Age skeleton with an amputated leg challenges modern understanding of prehistoric medicine

programme.title: Air Crash Investigation
programme.desc: An investigation into the crash of Continental Connection Flight 3407 in 2009. Fifty-one people died when it plummeted into a house in north-east Buffalo, 10km from the runway

programme.title: Inside Airport Lost & Found
programme.sub-title: A Cat on the Runway and a Runway Dress
programme.desc: Airport workers go above and beyond to find a cat who escaped onto the runway upon landing

programme.title: Alaska: The Next Generation
programme.desc: Johnny Rolfe must adopt the ways of the wolf to hunt caribou and fill his empty meat cache, while Kaleb Rowland helps a neighbour

programme.title: Made in a Day
programme.desc: Behind the scenes at the world's largest airline caterers, producing millions of meals from their Los Angeles kitchen to feed 40,000 people flying from LAX every day

programme.title: To Catch a Smuggler
programme.desc: A frequent visitor to Colombia is questioned at Miami International Airport. Meanwhile, past drug use comes back to haunt a passenger at JFK

programme.title: To Catch a Smuggler
programme.desc: An elderly woman arriving at JFK airport from Peru is supected of carrying drugs concealed in bottles. At MIA, a sting operation is carried out on a shipment of paintings

programme.title: Food Factory
programme.desc: Discover how fruit leather, addictive cheese curds and zingy guacamole are created from raw materials to finished products

programme.title: Food Factory
programme.desc: Discover how eco-friendly coffee pods, addictive gyoza dumplings and moon cheese are created from raw materials to finished products

programme.title: Prairie Dog Dynasty
programme.desc: As mating season comes to an end, one male moves quickly to protect a pregnant female from predators, while another gets carried away defending its territory

programme.title: NHK NEWSLINE
programme.desc: NHK NEWSLINE brings you up to date with the latest from Japan, Asia and around the world. Our team covers breaking news and major developments, with trusted anchors to tie it all together.

programme.title: MATSURI: The Heartbeat of Japan
programme.desc: Sawara Taisai looks back 300 years to a time when the town of Sawara was a vibrant cultural center. Large, elaborately decorated floats are paraded through the streets.

programme.title: Nun's Cookbook
programme.desc: The nuns of Otowasan Kannonji Temple show us how to make a simple fall treat that's both beautiful to look at and tasty to eat. Just boil edible chrysanthemums and serve with sweet vinegar.

programme.title: Journeys in Japan
programme.desc: Architect James Lambiasi trains his eye on Nagoya, the old castle town that flourished as a modern industrial hub from the 19th century. He traces the city's history through its architecture.

programme.title: NHK NEWSLINE
programme.desc: NHK NEWSLINE brings you up to date with the latest from Japan, Asia and around the world. Our team covers breaking news and major developments, with trusted anchors to tie it all together.

programme.title: Herbal Symphony short stories
programme.desc: In Uda, discover Japan's oldest private medicinal herb garden, where the natural landscape from 300 years ago is preserved in a botanical time capsule, a sanctuary of the local culture and history.

programme.title: The Masterpieces of Ukiyo-e producer Tsu
programme.desc: This miniseries presents the masterpieces of Tsutaju, a brilliant ukiyo-e producer of the Edo period. This episode spotlights ukiyo-e artist Sharaku's debut work The Actor Otani Oniji III as Edobei.

programme.title: Dining With the Chef
programme.desc: Wasabi isn't just for sushi! Add its spicy kick and fresh aroma to everyday dishes. Chef Rika introduces two recipes: salad with wasabi dressing, and pasta with wasabi butter soy sauce.

programme.title: NHK NEWSLINE
programme.desc: NHK NEWSLINE brings you up to date with the latest from Japan, Asia and around the world. Our team covers breaking news and major developments, with trusted anchors to tie it all together.

programme.title: CINEMATIC JOURNEY
programme.desc: Join our explorers as they pursue the cinematic beauty of Japan. Kyle Card hikes the newly designated long trail around majestic Mt. Fuji and discovers its secrets.

programme.title: Nun's Cookbook
programme.desc: The nuns of Otowasan Kannonji Temple show us how to make sesame-covered taro dumplings. Simply mash up boiled taro, add cheese, sprinkle with sesame, and deep fry for some tasty autumn goodness.

programme.title: Document 72 hours
programme.desc: Tokyo's Akihabara is a hub of maid cafe culture. Once catering mainly to male customers, these cafes now also attract women and families. For three days, we went inside to explore one cafe's appeal.

programme.title: NHK NEWSLINE
programme.desc: NHK NEWSLINE brings you up to date with the latest from Japan, Asia and around the world. Our team covers breaking news and major developments, with trusted anchors to tie it all together.

programme.title: CINEMATIC JOURNEY
programme.desc: Join our explorers as they pursue the cinematic beauty of Japan. Kyle Card hikes the newly designated long trail around majestic Mt. Fuji and discovers its secrets.

programme.title: Nun's Cookbook
programme.desc: The nuns of Otowasan Kannonji Temple show us how to make shiba-zuke pickles. Cucumbers, myoga, and a little bit of ume vinegar make the perfect side dish to go with newly harvested rice.

programme.title: Medical Frontiers
programme.desc: Adult spinal deformity (ASD) can develop due to age-related muscle loss or osteoporosis. We introduce ways to improve ASD through exercise therapy and explore AI-based efforts for early detection.

programme.title: NHK NEWSLINE
programme.desc: NHK NEWSLINE brings you up to date with the latest from Japan, Asia and around the world. Our team covers breaking news and major developments, with trusted anchors to tie it all together.

programme.title: MATSURI: The Heartbeat of Japan
programme.desc: Gataine Odori is a dance that depicts exhausting land reclamation work carried out in Omuta in the 19th century. A group of elderly women teach the dance to schoolchildren, and keep the story alive.

programme.title: On the Wings 5min.
programme.desc: Journey through the air on virtual excursions from Tokyo Haneda to regional airports all over Japan. This time it's New Ishigaki Airport; islands in an emerald sea from over 40,000ft.

programme.title: The Masterpieces of Ukiyo-e producer Tsu

programme.title: The Woman Who Came Back
programme.desc: 1945. Horror. Directed by Walter Colmes. Stars John Loder, Nancy Kelly And Otto Kruger. A woman returns to her hometown and becomes convinced that she has been possessed by a witch's spirit. [S]

programme.title: D.O.A. (1949)
programme.desc: 1949. Mystery. Directed by Rudolph Maté. Stars Edmond O'Brien, Pamela Britton And Luther Adler. An accountant learns that he has been poisoned, with only a few days to live, he hunts down his enemy. [S]

programme.title: The Lawless Years
programme.desc: The Immigrant. 1959. Stars James Gregory, Robert Karnes And Clu Gulager. An immigrant is pulled into bootlegging and Ruditsky investigates.

programme.title: The Punching Preacher
programme.desc: An insightful documentary by Peter Williams about George Foreman, a man of great faith who was known as one of the best fighters who ever lived, who twice held the World Heavyweight title. [S]

programme.title: Glencannon: The Loving Cup
programme.desc: 1959. Comedy. Stars Thomas Mitchell And Patrick Allen. A wonderful episode of the rare series about the adventures of Colin Glencannon, the chief engineer of the freighter Inchcliffe Castle. [S]

programme.title: The Veil
programme.desc: Summer Heat. 1958. Stars Boris Karloff, Harry Bartell And Paul Bryar. A man watches neighbours across a courtyard and believes he has witnessed a murder, no one will accept his disturbing claims. [S]

programme.title: The Man from U.N.C.L.E
programme.desc: The Love Affair. 1968. Stars Robert Vaughn, David McCallum And Leo G. Carroll. U.N.C.L.E investigates Brother Love, a religious figure who kidnaps leading scientists for a new Thrush operation. [S]

programme.title: Sherlock Holmes
programme.desc: The Case of the Cunningham Heritage. 1954. Starring: Ronald Howard, H. Marion Crawford And Archie Duncan. Sherlock and Watson investigate a murder, with a young lady as the prime suspect. [S]

programme.title: Captain Scarlett
programme.desc: 1953. Adventure. Director: Thomas Carr. Stars Richard Greene, Leonora Amar And Manolo Fabregas. Scarlett returns to France to find the Duke of Corlaine seizing property and terrorising resistors. [S]

programme.title: Star Performance: Here Comes the Suit
programme.desc: ...the Suit. 1955. Drama. Director: Richard Kinon. Stars David Niven, Jesse White, Allison Hayes. A timid businessman becomes the centre of attention after getting a new suit from a shady tailor. [S]

programme.title: Fighting Man of the Plains
programme.desc: 1949. Western. Stars Randolph Scott, Bill Williams And Victor Jory. Jim Dancer, one of Quantrill's Raiders, stages attacks on Kansas on behalf of the fallen Confederacy. [S]

programme.title: Crooks In Cloisters
programme.desc: 1964. Comedy. Director: Jeremy Summers. Stars Barbara Windsor, Bernard Cribbins, Melvyn Hayes. After pulling off the smallest train robbery, Little Walter and his crew decide to get out of London. [S]

programme.title: Scotland Yard
programme.desc: 1957. The Case of the Smiling Widow. Director: Montgomery Tully. Starring Russell Napier and Vernon Greeves. Police question the circumstances of an apparent death by taking one's own life. (S1, E22)

programme.title: William Tell
programme.desc: Gessler's Daughter. 1959. Stars Conrad Phillips, Jennifer Jayne And Willoughby Goddard. Gessler turns to William Tell for help when his daughter is kidnapped and held for ransom. [S]

programme.title: Lydia
programme.desc: 1941. Romance. Directed by Julien Duvivier. Stars Merle Oberon, Joseph Cotton And Edna May Oliver. Wealthy Lydia Macmillan meets three former suitors and together they relive the past thirty years. [S]

programme.title: Scotland Yard
programme.desc: 1954. The Mysterious Bullet. Directed by Paul Gherzo. Starring Robert Raglan, John Warwick and Christine Adrian. A ballistics expert tracks down the killer of a widow's fiance. (S1, E13)

programme.title: That's My Boy
programme.desc: Moving Out. 1985. Stars Mollie Sugden, Christopher Blake And Harold Goodwin. Robert has finally got an opportunity to work in a private practice. The only problem is it means moving to Yorkshire. [S]

programme.title: Passport To Treason
programme.desc: 1956. Crime Drama. Directed by Robert S. Baker. Stars Rod Cameron and Lois Maxwell. Clifford, an American private eye, stationed in London for the sake of a murdered friend, takes over a case. [S]

programme.title: Look At Life Women in Green
programme.desc: 1960. A look at the incredible Women's Voluntary Service. The women in green remain reliable and will always be first on the scene when disaster strikes in Britain.

programme.title: Whiplash
programme.desc: Act of Courage. 1961. Stars Peter Graves And Guy Doleman. While on his way to testify at the trial of a killer bushranger, Cobb stops at a way station, but a gang arrives to disrupt his plans. [S]

programme.title: The Man from U.N.C.L.E
programme.desc: The Cherry Blossom Affair. 1965. Stars Robert Vaughn, David McCallum And France Nuyen. THRUSH have acquired a volcano activating device. The team travel to Japan to find it before it's too late. [S]

programme.title: Buccaneer
programme.desc: Feet of Clay. 1980. Stars Bryan Marshall, Clifford Rose And Pamela Salem. Burton plots to exploit Redair's finances. The Britannia may be being tampered with. [S]

programme.title: Tiger in the Smoke
programme.desc: 1956. Drama. Director: Roy Ward Baker. Stars Donald Sinden And Muriel Pavlow. A young officer is killed during a raid to kill a German general at the house which belonged to his grandmother. [S]

programme.title: Zombies
programme.desc: Short documentary film detailing the contributions zombie films have made to the horror genre in the last 60 years, including Night Of The Living Dead and White Zombie, starring Bela Lugosi

programme.title: Fortean TV
programme.desc: 1997. Hosted by Reverend Lionel Fanthorpe. Tonight, there is a strange electrical interference, meet duster Jesus and Dolphin Man, discover a new animal species and visit a Thai Vegetarian Festival.

programme.title: Play for Today: Leeds United!
programme.desc: Leeds United! 1974. Stars Lynne Perrie, Elizabeth Spriggs And Lori Wells. The true story of a strike by female factory workers fighting for equal pay from their trade union in 1970. [S]

programme.title: Captain Apache
programme.desc: 1971. Western. Stars Lee Van Cleef, Carroll Baker And Stuart Whitman. A Native American becomes an Army officer tasked with investigating a murder. His only clue is buried in the victim's final words.

programme.title: Cinebox Memories
programme.desc: 1966. Enjoy this video of Bobby Rydell as he performs his wonderful song Bellazza.

programme.title: The Directors
programme.desc: Sam Peckinpah, a hard-hitting director who had seen atrocities at the end of the war as a marine became known for his violent scenes, he is remembered as the man who reinvented the western. [S]

programme.title: The Man from U.N.C.L.E
programme.desc: The Gazebo in the Maze Affair. 1965. Stars Robert Vaughn, David McCallum And Leo G. Carroll. G. Emory Partridge is seeking revenge on Solo and U.N.C.L.E for foiling a plot seven years earlier. [S]

programme.title: Sherlock Holmes

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E3The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt, a Second World War fighter aircraft produced by the American company Republic Aviation from 1941 until 1945. It was considered a successful high-altitude fighter and also served as the foremost US fighter-bomber in the ground-attack role.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E4The Yakovlev Yak-3, a Second World War Soviet fighter that was regarded for its performance at low altitudes and its agility. It was one of the most successful Soviet aircraft designs of the war.

programme.title: WWII Air Crash Detectives
programme.desc: E1February, 1943, a B-25 Mitchell Bomber crashes into Sharp Top Mountain. It was the third training crash in the area that night. What really caused this accident?

programme.title: WWII Air Crash Detectives
programme.desc: E6It is the 25th of August, 1942. A Short Sunderland Flying Boat slams into Eagle Rock, a remote hillside in the far north of Scotland, killing fourteen people on board. Miraculously, there is one survivor.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E4We examine the robot that defused bombs both on foreign battlefields and British streets, and an astonishing Gulf War minelayer.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E3Examining the machines used by iconic military unit 'The Desert Rats' in the North African desert campaign of World War II.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E1The F15 Eagle immediately turned the tide of the first Gulf War to prove its greatness. Our immaculately restored MiG Killer was involved in one of the most bizarre combat incidents during that conflict, and has survived to tell the tale.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E2The mighty Flying Fortress takes to the air as we examine the background and development of one of WWIIs most iconic bombers. Serving with both the USAAF and the RAF, we see it in action and fly a surfing example.

programme.title: Secret Wars Uncovered
programme.desc: E1In 1944, 28 Greek socialists were shot in Syntagma Square and 100,000 had perished by the end of the Civil War. Was this the old order Winston Churchill had longed for?

programme.title: Secret Wars Uncovered
programme.desc: E2Since the Syrian civil war broke out in 2011, 400,000 have been killed in the conflict. Who is to blame for this and the terrible conditions in which its people live?

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E1Nazi Germany boasted that its locomotives were faster and more innovative. This programme examines that claim by looking at these ‘flying trains’.

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E2Veterans and historians of the Thai-Burma railway tell the story of its construction. Built to supply Japan’s invasion of India, it cost thousands of lives – both POWs and Asian slave labourers.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E9The decision by Hitler to send his armies east in to Russia was probably the most significant of the war. Now against military convention, he was fighting on two fronts and almost as bad made a bitter enemy of an erstwhile ally.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E10And so it finally arrived: 6th June 1944, the day that British, US and Canadian troops were sent across the English Channel to begin the job of reclaiming continental Europe and freeing it from German occupation.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E7Meanwhile in North Africa, the Italian dictator Mussolini had his own ideas about building a new Roman Empire in the region. And so he sent thousands of poorly-trained and ill-prepared Italian troops against the British garrison in Egypt.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E8This episode remembers some of the thunderous naval battles which took place during the Pacific war. They include the Battle of the Coral Sea, the battle of Midway and the biggest naval engagement of the war – the battle of Leyte Gulf.

programme.title: Hitler's Coup 1923
programme.desc: E1Hitler’s Coup is the story around Hitler's Beer Hall Putsch, marking the first big attempt at taking over the German Chancellery with many of his key loyal servants in place: Herman Goering, Rudolf Hess & Heinrich Himmler.

programme.title: Hitler & Churchill: The Eagle & The Lion
programme.desc: E1The Old Lion vs. the German Eagle. This clash of titans waged at the highest level of power dominated the last century. And leads us to posit a chilling contingency to history: what would Europe be now had the players been different?

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E1Colditz Castle, the foreboding Nazi fortress that became a university of escapology; The Great Escape, and the doomed airmen of Stalag Luft Three; and the most daring breakout of them all, the ‘Warburg Wire Job’.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E6We trace the astonishing story of designers turning away from metal and back to wood to create a twin-engine bomber that could outrun almost any aircraft in the sky, yet deliver a bomb load greater than an Avro Lancaster.

programme.title: Combat Ships

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E3The German mass breakout that stunned wartime Britain, the astonishing secret behind the daring escape of an American bomber crew trapped in the Soviet Union, and the Trojan Horse of Stalag Luft Three.

programme.desc: E4The Russian soldier who led a desperate outbreak from a secret Nazi death camp, Operation Chicken - an audacious plan to flee an escape-proof Japanese prison camp, and the pilots whose bold bid for freedom won the admiration of their enemies.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E7A look at key maritime weapons such as the secret super-weapon that kept Constantinople safe for centuries, the thunderous force of a ship's cannon, and the deadly torpedo.

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E8Examining how the techniques of ambush, along with weapons that remained undetected until the very moment they were used, would revolutionise warfare.

programme.title: Combat Machines

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E5Exploring the machines that hide in the shadows, capturing, transmitting and analysing vital combat information.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E4Cruelly called 'the packing case the B17 came in,' the Liberator more than proved its worth over Europe and the Pacific, patterning the B17 to deliver a blow to the axis powers in WWII however it wasn't simply a bomb delivery system.

programme.title: Secret Wars Uncovered
programme.desc: E3In 2008, nearly 850 people are killed in the Russo-Georgian War. How did it erupt and what is the current relationship between the two nations?

programme.title: Secret Wars Uncovered

programme.title: History Of Weapons

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E10Experts look at three types of weapon employed to attack civilian populations, from the medieval trebuchet to modern bio-weapons and nuclear bombs.

programme.title: Hell On Earth: WWII
programme.desc: E8The bloodiest months of the war are still ahead. A Soviet surge pushes German forces back to within 30 kilometres of the Polish Border. The siege at Leningrad is lifted after 900 days and Operation Overlord, D-Day, opens a second front in Europe.

programme.title: Hell On Earth: WWII
programme.desc: E5The war enters its third year with battlefields in Eastern Europe, North Africa and the Asia/Pacific. The Battle of Midway, a battle with irreversible consequences, is a victory for the USA.

programme.desc: E5Stunning, newly colorised combat and newsreel footage plus personal memoirs take us to the heart of a battle that would be a catastrophic blow to both sides and leave a muddy graveyard across East Belgium.

programme.title: Erlebnisreisen: Peru
programme.desc: Peru ist viermal so groß wie Deutschland. Kaum ein anderes Land ist so vielfältig. Immo Mäueler hat den Andenstaat zwei Wochen lang bereist und faszinierende Aufnahmen mitgebracht.

programme.title: Der Mississippi - Die Seele Amerikas
programme.desc: Mit einer Länge von fast 4000 Kilometern ist der Mississippi zwar nicht der längste Fluss Nordamerikas, aber der bedeutendste. An den Ufern des gewaltigen Stromes leben seit mehreren Tausend Jahren Menschen. Als die Europäer kamen, verdrängten sie die einheimischen Völker. Heute vereint der Fluss viele Kulturen und ist die Seele Amerikas.

programme.title: Kanada - Die Rückkehr der Blackfoot
programme.desc: In der Provinz Alberta in Kanada ist die Landschaft in vielen Regionen noch unberührt und von atemberaubender Schönheit. Hier sind die Blackfoot zu Hause. Sie gehören zu den First Nations in Kanada. Ihr Stammesgebiet erstreckte sich einst über 160.000 Quadratkilometer, eine Fläche fast halb so groß wie Deutschland. Heutzutage sind die Blackfoot mit ihrer Kultur wieder in der Öffentlichkeit präsent. Sie leben ihre Rituale, feiern ihre Traditionen. Dazu gehören Staffelrennen mit Pferden, das sogenannte Indian Relay Racing.

programme.title: Am Pass - Geschichten aus der Spitzenküche
programme.desc: Spitzenküche auf einer Urlaubsinsel ist besonders anspruchsvoll. Besonders wichtig ist Kebschull die Arbeit mit dem Team.

programme.title: Natur im Garten (2/10)
programme.desc: Natur im Garten führt diesmal zum neugestalteten Nibelungenplatz in Tulln an der Donau. Karl Ploberger widmet sich farbenfrohen Blattschmuckpflanzen, Uschi stellt die Aroniabeere vor.

programme.title: Täuschen und Tarnen - Über Lebenskünstler der Natur
programme.desc: Das Motto Täuschen und Tarnen als Erfolgsprinzip der Evolution: Die Dokumentation zeichnet am Beispiel einer kleinen Vulkaninsel nach, wie sich Biotope und Populationen entwickeln.

programme.title: Die Magie der Mongolei
programme.desc: Im Herzen Asiens, isoliert von den Wäldern Sibiriens im Norden und der Chinesischen Mauer im Süden, liegt eine der schönsten und unberührtesten Naturlandschaften der Erde: die Mongolei.

programme.title: Extrem! Heißkalt - Die extremsten Orte der Welt
programme.desc: Das kälteste aller bewohnten Gebiete der Erde ist das Hochland von Oimjakon in Nordostsibirien. Werden die Bewohner dieser Dörfer zu den wenigen Gewinnern der Klimaerwärmung zählen?

programme.title: Extrem! Zwischen Dürre und Sintflut
programme.desc: Regenfälle mit 60 Litern Niederschlag in der Stunde in Österreich, tödliche Trockenheit dagegen am Horn von Afrika - das sind Ereignisse, die mögliche Klimaszenarien vor Augen führen.

programme.title: Extrem! Von höchsten Höhen bis unters Meer
programme.desc: In the near future, some of the settlement areas will become uninhabitable, and new land will need to be tapped into because of climate change. Are there any limitations to realizing the impossible? Filmmaker Udo Maurer's voyage through the world's extremes compares life at sea level with the highest mountains of the world. From the lagoons and palm beaches of the South Sea Islands whose highest peak is often only soem few meters high to the highlands of Ethiopia at four thousand metres. From the shores of Dead Sea, located at 408 meters below sea level, to the 5400 meter high La Rinconada, the gold minder city, in the Peruvian Andes. La Rinconada is not like any other place, it is the highest inhabited place on Earth. If someone dares to go that long stretch, it is only for one reason: to become rich. In fact, there is gold in La Rinconada - and that attracts adventurers from all over the world., In naher Zukunft werden einige der Siedlungsgebiete unbewohnbar werden, und aufgrund des Klimawandels müssen neue Flächen erschlossen werden. Gibt es Grenzen für die Verwirklichung des Unmöglichen? Filmemacher Udo Maurer reist durch die Extreme der Welt und vergleicht das Leben auf Meereshöhe mit den höchsten Bergen der Welt. Von den Lagunen und Palmenstränden der Südseeinseln, deren höchster Gipfel oft nur wenige Meter hoch ist, bis zum viertausend Meter hohen Hochland von Äthiopien. Von den Ufern des Toten Meeres, das 408 Meter unter dem Meeresspiegel liegt, bis zum 5400 Meter hohen La Rinconada, der Goldgräberstadt, in den peruanischen Anden. La Rinconada ist kein Ort wie jeder andere, es ist der höchste bewohnte Ort der Erde. Wenn sich jemand auf diese lange Strecke wagt, dann nur aus einem einzigen Grund: um reich zu werden. Tatsächlich gibt es in La Rinconada Gold - und das lockt Abenteurer aus aller Welt an.

programme.title: Extrem! - Licht und Schatten
programme.desc: Eine Reise zu den dunkelsten und hellsten bewohnten Orten der Welt: Dorthin, wo kaum jemals eine Wolke am Himmel zu sehen ist oder monatelang kein einziger Sonnenstrahl zum Boden vordringt.

programme.title: Bergauf-Bergab
programme.desc: Dichter Bergwald, darüber sanftes Wiesen und Almgelände: Die bayerischen Voralpen sind im Vergleich mit den hohen Alpengipfeln ein eher unspektakuläres Gebirge.

programme.title: Großbritanniens schönste Bahnstrecken (1/4)
programme.desc: Über hundert historische Museumsbahnen lassen in Großbritannien das Zeitalter der Dampflokomotiven aufleben. Eine davon ist die Lakeside And Haverthwaite-Linie der Familie Maher.

programme.title: Großbritanniens schönste Bahnstrecken (2/4)
programme.desc: Das britische Eisenbahnnetz ist das älteste der Welt. In Museumsbahnen wie der Keighley And Worth Valley-Linie lebt seine ruhmreiche Vergangenheit dank Helfern wie Heizer Tom weiter.

programme.title: Großbritanniens schönste Bahnstrecken (3/4)
programme.desc: Die Black-Five gehören zu den legendärsten Dampflokomotiven Großbritanniens. Nach Restaurierung kehrt eine Maschine in den Dienst der schottischen Strathspey-Museumsbahn zurück.

programme.title: Großbritanniens schönste Bahnstrecken (4/4)
programme.desc: Bei der Keigley And Worth Valley-Museumslinie steht ein großes Jubiläum an: 1970 wurde dort der britische Klassiker The Railway Children gedreht. Star des Films: eine ganze bestimmte Lok.

programme.title: Auf Schmugglers Pfaden – Die Wegbereiter Englands (1/3)
programme.desc: An der waldbewachsenen Küste Somersets beginnt der Schmugglerweg. Das artenreiche Hochmoor ist Heimat wilder Exmoor-Ponys und seltener Rothirsche. Der South West Coast Path führt durch die uralten Wälder von Culbone, über die weißen Sandstrände von Putsborough und durch die farbenfrohe Dünenlandschaft bis hin zur schroffen Küste von Hartland.

programme.title: Auf Schmugglers Pfaden – Die Wegbereiter Englands (2/3)
programme.desc: Cornwall im Süden Englands zählt zu den schönsten und vielfältigsten Grafschaften der Insel. Die atemberaubenden Landschaften bieten ein abwechslungsreiches Ökosystem und schaffen besondere klimatische Bedingungen. Berühmt für traditionelle Sport- und Handwerksstätten, ist Cornwall ein Mekka für Kunstschaffende. Der alte Schmugglerweg hat hier ganz besondere Menschen angezogen.

programme.title: Auf Schmugglers Pfaden – Die Wegbereiter Englands (3/3)
programme.desc: Süd-Devon und Dorset bilden die letzten Etappen des über 1000 Kilometer langen South West Coast Path. Die beiden Grafschaften bestechen durch kontrastreiche Lebensräume, prähistorische Spuren und eine reiche kulturelle Tradition. Doch es sind die Menschen entlang des Schmugglerwegs, die Geschichte und Brauchtum lebendig halten und in die Zukunft tragen.

programme.title: nano
programme.desc: Die Welt von morgen

programme.title: heute
programme.desc: Die heute ist eine Nachrichtensendung des ZDF mit aktuellen Meldungen des Tages aus den Bereichen Politik, Wirtschaft, Wissenschaft, Kultur, Gesellschaft, Sport und Wetter. Die Sendung informiert kompakt und verständlich über die wichtigsten Ereignisse im In- und Ausland und ordnet diese journalistisch ein. Ergänzt wird sie durch Hintergrundberichte, Live-Schalten und Korrespondentenbeiträge. Durch ihre klare Struktur und verlässliche Berichterstattung gehört sie zu den festen Informationsformaten im deutschen Fernsehen und bietet täglich einen schnellen Überblick über das aktuelle Geschehen.

programme.title: 3sat-Wetter
programme.desc: 3sat zeigt das Wetter aus den 3sat-Ländern Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz.

programme.title: Kulturzeit
programme.desc: Das 3sat-Kulturmagazin von ZDF, ORF, SRF und ARD

programme.title: Tagesschau
programme.desc: ARD-Nachrichten aus dem In- und Ausland auf den Punkt gebracht.

programme.title: Dirty Money - Geldwäsche Paradies Deutschland
programme.desc: 'Dirty Money - Geldwäsche-Paradies Deutschland' zeigt, wie Milliarden aus Drogenhandel, Terrornetzwerken und organisierter Kriminalität täglich in den deutschen Wirtschaftskreislauf fließen. Der Film verfolgt die Spur des schmutzigen Geldes, enthüllt Tricks der Geldwäscher und gewährt exklusive Einblicke in die Arbeit von BKA, Zoll und Steuerfahndung. Eindrücklich wird klar, warum konsequente Geldwäschebekämpfung mehr ist als Finanzpolitik - sie ist eine Frage der nationalen Sicherheit.

programme.title: Erlebnisreisen: Apulien
programme.desc: Eine Rundreise durch Apulien führt vom südlichen Salento mit der Hafenstadt Otranto durch endlose Olivenhaine nach Ostuni.

programme.title: ZIB 2
programme.desc: Das tägliche Nachrichtenmagazin des ORF-Fernsehens.

programme.title: Der Bankraub
programme.desc: Der verzweifelte Arbeiter Werner Kreye fährt mit seinem Auto in voller Absicht auf den Chefbanker Draeger zu, der seinem Sohn Martin zu einer internationalen Karriere verholfen hat.

programme.title: 10 vor 10
programme.desc: 10 vor 10 ist eine Informationssendung von Schweizer Radio und Fernsehen (SRF).

programme.title: STÖCKL
programme.desc: Barbara Stöckl lädt wöchentlich große Persönlichkeiten des Jetzt zum Gespräch und nimmt das Publikum mit auf eine sehr persönliche Reise ins Spannungsfeld zwischen Geschichte und Zukunft, zwischen Resümee und Vision, zwischen Erfahrungsschatz und unbekümmertem Zukunftsglauben.

programme.title: Alte Liebe rostet nicht - Die wachsende Leidenschaft für Oldtimer
programme.desc: Wenn Silvia O. ihr Käfer-Cabrio aus der Garage holt, dann wird für die Ausfahrt das Fahrzeug nicht nur geputzt, sondern auch eine frische Blume in die serienmäßig verbaute Vase gesteckt, die in den 1950er und -60er Jahren als ein Symbol für Individualität und Lebensfreude verstanden wurde. Nachdem viele Oldtimer-Liebhaber, wie Christian S., den Winter zum Schrauben nützen, beginnen mit den ersten sonnigen Wochenenden im ganzen Land die Ausfahrten mit den Lieblingen aus Blech.

programme.title: Animal Cops Philadelphia
programme.desc: Kun harjoittelija-agentti Derrick Schlitter vastaa hätäpuheluun Pohjois-Philadelphiassa, hän päätyy hakemaan oikeutta takapihalle kuolleena jätetylle pennulle.

programme.title: Alaskan Bush People
programme.desc: Alaskan erämaassa elää seitsenlapsinen Brownin perhe. He asuvat yhteiskunnan ulkopuolella ilman mukavuuksia, ja luonnon armoilla he ovat täysin riippuvaisia toisistaan.

programme.title: My Cat From Hell
programme.desc: Taran kissa Cali rakastaa omistajaansa, mutta hyökkää vierailijan päälle. Kurtin kissa Kurtis Jr tuhoaa ja syö kaiken tieltään. Kissojen käytöstuntija Jackson Galaxy saapuu apuun.

programme.title: Pandamonium
programme.desc: Kevään kiima-aika on alkanut, ja vuosittain täytyy syntyä 15 pentua pandapopulaation säilymiseksi. Matkaamme myös Qinling-vuorille tarkkailemaan villipandoja.

programme.title: Das schwarze Quadrat
programme.desc: Die Kunstdiebe Vincent und Nils haben das berühmte russische Gemälde Das schwarze Quadrat gestohlen. Das Bild soll auf einem Kreuzfahrtschiff an den Käufer übergeben werden. Um auf das Schiff zu kommen, überwältigen sie kurzerhand zwei Passagiere.

programme.title: Die Queen und ich
programme.desc: Über ihren Tod hinaus ist Königin Elizabeth II. die berühmteste Frau der Welt. Doch wie sie dachte und empfand, was sie bewegte und inspirierte, blieb ein Geheimnis. Die Queen und ich kommt der legendären Monarchin näher denn je. Die Privatsekretärin, der Freund, der Bischof, der Schneider – erstmals teilen Vertraute aus dem Inner Circle ihre Erinnerungen an die Queen.

programme.title: Die Mythen der Wikinger
programme.desc: Um zu erfahren, was die Zukunft für die Götter Asgards und die anderen Kreaturen des Universums bereithält, muss Göttervater Odin eine schreckliche Prüfung bestehen: Neun Tage und neun Nächte lang wird er am Weltenbaum Yggdrasil hängen, ohne zu essen oder zu trinken. Wenn er Wissen erlangen will, muss er zudem sein linkes Auge opfern. Als er wieder zu sich kommt, hört er ein Wort, das das Schicksal des Universums besiegeln wird: „Ragnarök“.

programme.title: Mit offenen Augen
programme.desc: Bild ist Sprache: die vorherrschende Sprache unserer Welt. Bilder sind mächtig und allgegenwärtig. Wir alle sind tagtäglich einer Flut von Bildern ausgesetzt, die wir mehr oder weniger bewusst wahrnehmen. Was wir sehen, kann schockieren oder bewegen. Aber verstehen wir immer auf den ersten Blick, was wir sehen? Sonia Devillers ordnet Bilder ein und erklärt Hintergründe.

programme.title: 28 Minuten
programme.desc: Bücherherbst: Ananda Devi veröffentlicht ihr neues Werk, Chronique d’un royaume perdu (Chronik eines verlorenen Königreichs, Grasset). / Russische Bedrohung: Emmanuel Macron traf die ersten Freiwilligen des neuen nationalen Dienstes, der als Antwort auf neue sicherheitspolitische Bedrohungen präsentiert wird.

programme.title: 360° Reportage
programme.desc: Mit ihren gewagten Sprüngen und Pirouetten brettern sie gegen hartnäckig fortbestehende Klischees. Ihre Tracht soll provozieren und zeigen, dass den Cholitas heute alles offensteht. Dass sie sich dabei ausgerechnet auf Skateboards schwingen, löst Erstaunen aus. Doch die jungen Bolivianerinnen haben diesen Sport mit Bedacht gewählt ...

programme.title: Küchen der Welt
programme.desc: Maniok nach ivorischer Art: Placali mit Okra-Soße / Ein Biss'chen Heimat: Batty, eine Ivorerin in Toulouse / Ran an die Töpfe!

In dieser Folge: Madrid: Almudena Grandes' kleine Helden / Algier: Hauptstadt der Chaâbi-Musik / Sri Lanka: Padmalathas Fisch-Curry / Paris: Die Launen der Seine

programme.title: Der Orient-Express - Vintage auf Schienen
programme.desc: ARTE entdeckt den Orient: An Bord des Orientexpress geht es an die Grenzen Europas, Afrikas und Asiens. Die Traumreise folgt dem Nil auf den Spuren der Märchen von Tausendundeiner Nacht und lässt Aladin und die Wunderlampe oder auch die Abenteuer von Sindbad dem Seefahrer lebendig werden. Entlang der berühmten Seidenstraße führt der Weg durch Zentralasien zwischen Iran und Indien. Im Orient begegnen sich verschiedene Religionen – er ist die Wiege des Christentums und des Islam. Entdecken Sie die Wege des Orients am 20. Mai auf ARTE.

programme.title: Die Eisenbahn - Motor des Fortschritts
programme.desc: Seit etwa 200 Jahren gibt es die Eisenbahn – sie ist ein bahnbrechendes Transportmittel der Menschheit geworden. Ihr Siegeszug hat Gesellschaften, Landschaften und Städte verändert und ganze Länder ins Industriezeitalter katapultiert. Sie revolutionierte den Transport und demokratisierte das Reisen. Doch sie war auch ein Werkzeug der Kolonialmächte zur Ausbeutung und transportierte Menschen in den geplanten Tod in Auschwitz.

programme.title: Re ARTE
programme.desc: Italiens traditionelle Zeitungskioske, sind seit jeher Orte, an denen sich Anwohner treffen, um Zeitungen zu kaufen und sich über ihren Alltag auszutauschen. Doch in den letzten 15 Jahren sind zwei Drittel der kleinen Geschäfte verschwunden. Die Gründe dafür liegen an der Digitalisierung des Zeitungsmarktes. Bürger kämpfen darum, verbliebene Kioske zu erhalten - mit Erfolg.

programme.desc: Der Festtagseintopf aus Polynesien: Pua'a choux / Kulinarische Mitbringsel / Ran an die Töpfe!

programme.title: Mord im Mittsommer
programme.desc: Ein Raubüberfall wird zu einer Kindesentführung, als die Diebe ein Boot stehlen, auf dem sich ein Mädchen aus reichem Hause befindet. Doch das Kind ist schwer krank und wird ohne Medikamente sterben. Alexander und Valpen nehmen sich des Falls an – ohne zu ahnen, dass die Diebe auch Nora in ihrer Gewalt haben. Mord im Mittsommer, die Krimiserie zur gleichnamigen Romanreihe.

programme.title: GEO Reportage
programme.desc: Ganz an der Spitze der bretonischen Halbinsel liegt das Departement Finistère – übersetzt bedeutet das so viel wie Das Ende der Welt. Es ist eine urwüchsige Landschaft mit rauer Küste. Der Atlantik mit seinem Reichtum an Arten sicherte den Fischern traditionell ein gutes Auskommen, aber die Bestände gehen immer weiter zurück. Auch die Jagd nach dem Wolfsbarsch wird schwieriger.

programme.title: Mit dem Zug entlang der irischen Ostküste
programme.desc: Lange Strände, spektakuläre Klippen, einsame Berge: Von Rosslare im Südosten über die Hauptstadt Dublin bis zur Halbinsel Howth führt die wohl schönste Zugstrecke der Republik Irland. Die Gegend wurde geprägt von Normannen, Wikingern und der bewegten Geschichte mit England. Das Filmteam begegnet Menschen, die das moderne Land verkörpern und gleichzeitig weiter auf den Spuren ihrer Vorfahren unterwegs sind.

programme.title: Mit dem Zug durch Ungarn
programme.desc: Ungarn, das kleine Land in Mitteleuropa eignet sich besonders für eine Entdeckungsreise mit der Bahn. Unsere Fahrt führt vom Plattensee, im Westen des Landes, über Budapest bis ganz in den Osten, eine äußerst abwechslungsreiche Reise, bei der wir ein Büffelreservat genauso besuchen wie das größte Musik-Festivals Ungarns. Wir gehen schwimmen in einem einzigartigen Höhlenschwimmbad und erfahren, warum die Ungarn im Wasserball besonders gut sind.

programme.title: Mit dem Zug durch Hokkaido
programme.desc: Blumenfelder und rauchende Vulkane – Kontraste prägen das Bild Hokkaidos, der nördlichen Hauptinsel Japans. Mit dem Lavendelexpress geht es zu den Blumenfeldern Furanos und zum Akan-Nationalpark, wo noch die Ainu, die Ureinwohner der Insel, leben. Hokkaido ist eine Vielfalt aus grandioser Natur und Metropolen.

programme.title: Phänomenale Natur
programme.desc: Vor 15 Millionen Jahren entstand die japanische Insel Yakushima im Ostchinesischen Meer durch vulkanische Aktivität. Ihre Abgelegenheit und das Fehlen großer Raubtiere schufen ein einzigartiges Ökosystem: Hier leben endemische Unterarten japanischer Makaken und Sikahirsche, die Hochlagen sind von uralten japanischen Zedern geprägt. Heute steht der Schutz des Naturjuwels im Fokus.

programme.title: ARTE Journal
programme.desc: ARTE Journal, das europäische Nachrichtenmagazin, wirft einen aktuellen, weltoffenen und europäischen Blick auf Politik und Kultur.

programme.title: Mit offenen Karten - Im Fokus
programme.desc: Deutschland im Umbruch: Nach dem Sieg der rechtsextremen AfD am 6. September in Sachsen-Anhalt wurde am Sonntag in Berlin gewählt: Die Linke bekam die meisten Stimmen, Friedrich Merz' CDU wurde auf die Plätz verwiesen. In Mecklenburg-Vorpommern gewann knapp vor der SPD die AfD - sie konnte ihr Wahlergebnis von 2021 verdoppeln.

programme.title: Re ARTE
programme.desc: Die Comté-Produktion geht zu Lasten der Flüsse im Juragebirge. Wie kann man die erfolgreiche Produktion Frankreichs beliebtester Käsesorte beibehalten, ohne dabei das Ökosystem zu gefährden? Menschen vor Ort suchen nach Lösungen, um weiterhin Landwirtschaft zu betreiben und gleichzeitig das biologische Gleichgewicht zu wahren.

programme.title: Die Inquisition
programme.desc: Im 13. Jahrhundert schuf die katholische Kirche die Inquisition: eine mächtige Maschinerie, um Andersdenkende zu unterdrücken. Denunziationen, Verhaftungen und Hinrichtungen waren Teil eines perfiden Systems. Dieser Apparat professionalisierte sich durch Ermittlungen, Zeugenbefragungen und erzwungene Geständnisse. Ein Überwachungssystem, dessen Methoden bis heute nachwirken.

programme.title: Die Inquisition
programme.desc: Zu Beginn der Inquisition handelten die Gesandten der katholischen Kirche noch unabhängig voneinander in den Gebieten, für die sie vom Papst eingesetzt worden waren. Gegen Ende des 15. Jahrhunderts änderte sich das: Spanien, Portugal und Italien schufen zentralisierte und hierarchisch organisierte Behördenapparate. Und die Liste der Verfolgten wurde immer länger.

programme.title: Notre-Dame, die Jahrhundertbaustelle
programme.desc: Am 15. April 2019 stand eines der berühmtesten Wahrzeichen Frankreichs in Flammen: die Pariser Kathedrale Notre-Dame. Das Großfeuer durchdrang auch die Gewölbe und schwächte die Kalksteinmauern. Nach einjährigen Aufräum- und Sicherungsarbeiten war die Einsturzgefahr gebannt, die historisch originalgetreue Rekonstruktion der Kathedrale konnte beginnen.

programme.title: Notre-Dame, die Jahrhundertbaustelle
programme.desc: Eineinhalb Jahre nach dem Brand von Notre-Dame beschäftigt die mit der Restaurierung beauftragten Architekten und Wissenschaftler vor allem eines: die Stabilität der Gewölbe von Notre-Dame. Durch Modellierung der Kirchenstruktur entdecken sie die bewegte Baugeschichte der Kathedrale und verstehen, woraus das Gebäude seine große Widerstandskraft bezog.

programme.title: Notre-Dame, die Jahrhundertbaustelle
programme.desc: Von der Struktur und von den Proportionen her war Notre-Dame ein Wunderwerk: Höhe, Licht und Akustik spielten so harmonisch ineinander, dass der Besucher in den Genuss eines wahren Sinneserlebnisses gelangte. Im Innenraum der Kirche stand eine der berühmtesten Orgeln überhaupt. Doch auch in der Tiefe offenbart die Kathedrale einen Teil ihrer Geschichte, seitdem dort archäologische Ausgrabungen gemacht wurden.

programme.title: Adoptivkinder - Skandal ohne Grenzen
programme.desc: Hinter einer Wohltätigkeitsfassade hat sich das internationale Adoptionswesen seit den 1980er Jahren zu einem lukrativen Markt entwickelt. Grenzüberschreitende Adoptionen bleiben undurchsichtig. Auch schmutzige Praktiken begünstigen den Kinderhandel. Die Doku recherchiert unter anderem in Südkorea, dem Versuchslabor des internationalen Adoptionswesens, und in Schweden.

programme.title: Kühlung für die Erde - Wie holen wir das CO2 aus der Luft?
programme.desc: Unser Planet wird wärmer – das ist klar. Wie können wir ihn kühlen? Der Film zeigt, wie weltweit innovative Verfahren erprobt werden und lässt sie von führenden Klimaforschenden bewerten: Helfen riesige Filteranlagen in Island oder Gesteinsmehl auf unseren Äckern, wie es in Bayern getestet wird..?

programme.title: Mit Kompass und Köpfchen auf hoher See
programme.desc: Mit dem Katamaran „Nomade des Mers“ und seiner Crew macht sich der junge Ingenieur Corentin de Chatelperron zu einer Weltreise von Concarneau über Indonesien bis nach Südamerika auf, um autarke Lowtech-Lebensweisen zu erforschen. Lowtech ist Technik, die man überall günstig selbst bauen und reparieren kann. Während seiner Reise trifft er auf geniale lokale Erfinder praktischer und nachhaltiger Innovationen. Eine abenteuerliche Weltreise, die zum ökologischen Umdenken anregen soll.

programme.title: Mit offenen Augen
programme.desc: Ein Blick hinter die Kulissen der Macht: Anlässlich der 250 Jahre Unabhängigkeit der USA führt Influencerin Kai Trump ihre Follower durch das Weiße Haus. Versprochen wird Authentizität. Dahinter versteckt sich jedoch die Gelegenheit, aus der Amtszeit ihres Großvaters Profit zu schlagen.

programme.title: 28 Minuten
programme.desc: Mon frère: Ab dem 18. September ist das Stück Mon frère (Mein Bruder) von François und Christian Gremaud im Théâtre du Rond-Point in Paris zu sehen. François und sein von Geburt an gehörloser Bruder Christian schildern darin den Alltag eines Menschen ohne Gehör. / EU-Kommissionspräsidentin Ursula von der Leyen will Kanada zum ersten assoziierten Mitglied der EU machen.

programme.title: Auf den Spuren der Cheops-Pyramide
programme.desc: Die Cheops-Pyramide gehört zu den Pyramiden von Gizeh, dem einzigen noch erhaltenen Weltwunder der Antike. Sie wird auch als Große Pyramide bezeichnet und wurde vor über 4.500 Jahren im westlichen Niltal, etwa 25 Kilometer von Kairo entfernt, als Grabmal des Königs Cheops erbaut. Wie konnten die Ägypter ohne moderne Werkzeuge ein derart monumentales Bauwerk errichten?

programme.title: 360° Reportage
programme.desc: Ayuko Kamimura ist eine der besten Yabusame-Schützinnen der Welt. Die 51-Jährige ist die erste Frau, die von den konservativen Hütern der traditionellen Zeremonie als Lehrmeisterin anerkannt wurde. Jedes Jahr organisiert sie das Sakura-Turnier, das einzige Frauen-Event im Yabusame. Dort will sie nun ein letztes Mal vor grossem Publikum antreten – und gleichzeitig eine Nachfolgerin finden. Etwa die talentierte Aoi Fuse oder das 14-jährige Ausnahmetalent Eri Sakuraba.
